title: The Silent Crown Anew
premise: Ada Villalobos, a mercenary bound to the Silent God, has spent her life in the valley where magic cannot follow—until she finds her own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies. Hunted by the court beneath the mountain, she learns her soul was sold before her birth, and that the last dragon-fire keeping the Silent God's silence intact is guttering out. With a disgraced court scribe and a dragon who chose exile, Ada descends beneath the mountain to steal back what was sold, discovering that the Silent God never went silent at all—it was silenced by the crown itself. In the end, Ada must choose between reclaiming her stolen soul and using it to reignite the dragon-fire, burning away both the corrupt court and her own claim to a normal life; she gives up her soul, becomes the new vessel of the god's voice, and walks out of the valley for the first time.
about_author: Mirabel Vasquez is a former archivist of rare manuscripts who spent a decade cataloguing failed prophecies in mountain monasteries before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people whom history tried to erase, from a cabin full of unlabeled maps.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: POV Ada. On the eve of a rare date with the ferryman's daughter, Ada takes a routine contract hunting a wight at the valley's edge, where her god-sworn blade still works. The job goes wrong when the wight speaks her name. Emotional beat: restless contentment cracked open by the first hint that the world knows she exists.

chapters.title: A Date Written a Century Ago
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Her date ends abruptly when the girl's grandmother recognizes Ada from an old prophecy book: her face, tonight's date, inked a hundred years past. Ada burns the page; the ash spells her name again. Emotional beat: dread masquerading as denial.

chapters.title: The Scribe Who Fell Downhill
chapters.summary: POV Tam (the disgraced court scribe). Fleeing the court beneath the mountain for falsifying records, Tam carries the original prophecy book and lands half-dead in Ada's valley. He begs sanctuary, revealing the court hunts 'the Unwritten One.' Emotional beat: desperate charm over fear.

chapters.title: What the Blade Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Interrogating Tam by firelight, Ada learns her mercenary order was founded to guard something—not someone—and that her god went silent the year she was born. She tests her blade against his truth-sense; it hums. Emotional beat: grief for a childhood built on lies.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Court riders breach the valley's edge—the first magic ever to cross it, riding on Ada's unraveling anonymity. A skirmish kills two villagers. Ada realizes staying means burying everyone she loves. Emotional beat: guilt hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada says goodbye to Sefa, who refuses to be protected and instead gives her a river-stone that 'remembers directions home.' Their parting is tender and unfinished. Emotional beat: love as a reason to leave, not stay.

chapters.title: The Book of Small Prophecies
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Reading the prophecy book properly for the first time, Tam finds it isn't grand destiny—it's a ledger of small sold things, including 'a soul, unnamed, sold twice.' The final entry names the price of silence. Emotional beat: horror at bureaucratic evil.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Guided by the ledger, they reach a cave where Vess, an exiled dragon, tends a flame so small it fits in a cupped hand. Vess explains: the dragon-fire holds the god's silence in place, and when it dies, everything sold to the court comes due. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: Sold Twice
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Tam deciphers that Ada's soul was sold once by her parents' generation and bought back by the Silent God—which is why the god went silent: it spent its voice as payment. Ada is the receipt. Emotional beat: identity shattered and strangely freed.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The three descend through the mountain's old trade roads, dodging soul-tolls and memory-fog that makes travelers forget why they're walking. Ada ties Sefa's river-stone to her wrist. Emotional beat: claustrophobic determination.

chapters.title: The Toll of Names
chapters.summary: POV Tam. At a bridge guarded by a toll-keeper who eats spoken names, Tam sacrifices his family name to buy passage—an act that erases him from every record he ever falsified, freeing him and unmaking him. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the cost of self.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Ada. They enter the court: a glittering bureaucracy of souls filed like coins, presided over by the Regent of Quiet Things, who wears the Silent God's stolen voice as a necklace. Emotional beat: revulsion dressed as wonder.

chapters.title: An Audience of Ledgers
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Recognized despite his erased name, Tam bargains with the Regent, buying time by offering the prophecy book. Ada plays the mercenary hireling, getting close enough to see her soul: a small grey ember in a glass drawer. Emotional beat: terror under a mask of compliance.

chapters.title: The Drawer of Grey Embers
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Alone in the archive, Ada finds not one but hundreds of embers matching her description—souls sold across generations to keep the god silent. She takes hers; the alarm is a soundless bell that all souls feel. Emotional beat: theft as self-recognition.

chapters.title: The Necklace of Voices
chapters.summary: POV Vess. Vess reveals the truth she fled: the Regent was once the god's first priest, who strangled the divine voice and wore it. The dragon-fire wasn't holding silence in place—it was keeping the Regent's theft hidden. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing everything.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Filing Halls
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Hunted through endless archive halls, the three run as freed embers swirl around them like startled birds. Tam is captured buying their escape. Emotional beat: adrenaline laced with abandonment-guilt.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence Comes Due
chapters.summary: POV Tam. In the Regent's chamber, Tam learns the prophecy's final line: when the last dragon-fire gutters out, either the thief returns what was stolen or the silence devours the world. The Regent offers Tam Ada's freedom for the book. Emotional beat: temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: What Ada Cannot Keep
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Outside, with the ember in hand, Ada feels herself becoming whole—and discovers a whole soul cannot carry the god's voice; only a hollow one can. Reclaiming herself means dooming the world to the devouring silence. Emotional beat: the cruelest choice made flesh.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: POV Vess. The dragon-fire dies. Across the land, the silence begins to eat sound, names, memory. Vess offers her remaining life to hold the dark for one night. Emotional beat: sacrifice without heroics, just stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Crown Anew
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada returns beneath the mountain, confronts the Regent, and shatters the necklace of voices—but instead of taking her soul back, she pours it into the dead flame, becoming the vessel through which the Silent God speaks again. The Regent unravels into paperwork and dust. Emotional beat: climax as surrender that wins.

chapters.title: The Voice That Walks
chapters.summary: POV Tam. The god speaks through Ada now—quietly, in her own rough accent. Tam, nameless but free, begins writing a new book: not prophecies, but records of everything the court destroyed. Emotional beat: mourning braided with purpose.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada returns to the valley one last time, gives Sefa the truth and a choice, and walks out past the ridgeline as the god's quiet voice—for the first time in a century—says her name aloud. Emotional beat: bittersweet arrival; invisibility traded for a self worth being seen.
